newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile, Argentina to hold joint military manoeuvres.
newsitem.headline: Chile, Argentina to hold joint military manoeuvres.

text.p: Chilean and Argentine armed forces will carry out their first joint military manoeuvres next year in an important strengthening of bilateral defence ties, Argentine Defence Minister Jorge Dominguez said on Thursday.

"Chile and Argentina have taken the political decision that armed forces from both countries will take part in a wide-ranging exercise in the first half of 1998," Dominguez said at a news conference held by the Argentine and Chilean foreign and defence ministers.

Chile and Argentina, which share one of the world's longest borders, came close to war in 1978 over three islands in the southern Beagle Channel. The dispute was finally settled in 1984 with a Vatican-mediated treaty.
A treaty to settle the last outstanding border spat between the two countries, over an area of the southern Andes known as Laguna del Desierto, has yet to be passed by Congress in either country.
